evidence_quotes.quote: The methodological design followed a two-stage explorative research process where stakeholders were identified and classified based on an iterative process that drew on a combination of methods (e.g. 6 expert opinions - semi-structured interviews in English and Portuguese; ethnographic observations in 16 municipalities involving 40 user families)

The work identifies key players and issues influencing governance for the implementation of rainwater systems; and capture of decision making powers by agents making evident redundancies in the management of rainwater in the region; highlighting issues of lack of inclusion in the decision-making process, planning and implementation; threatening the sustainability, resilience and governance of rainwater systems in Belem.

A second effect of the centralization in the Brazilian federal model is expressed in the street bureaucracies which have a high degree of discretion and can, at the time of implementing the policy, change their nature or implementation protocols provided by the national body.

This type of capture of the policy for a supply of a water harvesting system by a bureaucracy with no technical capacity in sanitation increases the complexity of the bureaucracy in the implementation of the system since training for the maintenance of the system is not offered by SEASTER but depends on the technical knowledge allocated to the UFPA.

evidence_quotes.criterion: mechanism_certainty (lack of public agency monitoring and maintenance)
evidence_quotes.quote: As detected in the interactions with experts and the communities, the monitoring and infrastructure maintenance is deficient and not connected in any form with governmental agencies.
Social learning process hindered; uncovered expectations in terms of number of units implemented; failure / abandonment of several installed units

effect_estimate.comment: Accepted repository manuscript contains full text and Tables 1-2; Figures 1-3 are insertion placeholders, and no numeric SNA centrality scores or statistical estimates are printed anywhere in the text or tables.
effect_estimate.value: Qualitative — no numeric effect estimate reported. Governance of rooftop rainwater harvesting (RTRWH) implementation in Belém's island communities is constrained by total dependence on federal public funding, street-level bureaucratic policy capture and competition over resources (notably regional social assistance agency SEASTER capturing water/sanitation roles despite lacking technical sanitation capacity, alongside municipal regulator AMAE), overlapping multi-level agency roles, lack of governmental post-delivery monitoring and maintenance, and exclusion of recipient communities and local water/material traders from planning and governance rule-making. These institutional weaknesses create dependency on external brokers (UFPA and CARITAS), collective-action conflicts over shared maintenance, non-resilient service delivery, and failure or abandonment of several installed RTRWH units.

mechanism_certainty.comment: Rated 2 (mechanism directly observed empirically, at the maximum ceiling of 2 for a qualitative CASP study): expert interviews, focus group discussion, and ethnographic observations across 40 families in 16 municipalities directly document street-level bureaucratic intermediation/capture, lack of post-delivery public agency monitoring, and absent participatory maintenance governance affecting RTRWH operation and abandonment.
